clue.text: Empty container found outside prison

indicators.note: one thing found outside another wraps around it, so the vessel encloses the jail word

parts.note: a vat is a large tank or tub
the can is slang for jail

explanation.surface: An abandoned bin is discovered just beyond the walls of a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The can is American slang for prison, familiar from films.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacant room or seat is unoccupied, which is a straightforward synonym of empty.

clue.text: Incomplete picture put up in plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top
something incomplete is missing its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a mural is a picture painted on a wall

explanation.surface: Someone hangs an unfinished painting in a pot plant, which makes little sense as a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: MURAL loses its last letter to give MURA, which is then read upwards as ARUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a lily-like flowering plant with a hooded spathe, such as cuckoo-pint.

clue.text: No two Z's mixed shortly in this part of the world

definitions.text: No two Z's mixed shortly in this part of the world

parts.note: surface reading: an instruction about scrambling letters, with no Z appearing twice

parts.words: in this part of the world
parts.note: setter's reading: the letters N, O, Z and Z mixed spell the short names of New Zealand and Australia

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a region of the globe where you never see a pair of Z's.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix N, O and two Z's and you get NZ and OZ, the abbreviations ('shortly') for New Zealand and Australia, which together are what Britons call the Antipodes.
explanation.definitionFit: Britons call Australia and New Zealand the Antipodes because they lie on the opposite side of the globe.

clue.text: Agreement as a result of pleasant surprise unknown

parts.note: a treat is an unexpected pleasure
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A deal is reached thanks to a nice surprise from a mysterious source.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal pact between nations, so it is a kind of agreement.

clue.text: Rather hairy question asked about skier in difficulties

indicators.note: the question word is placed about, that is around, the other letters

parts.note: why is a question word

indicators.note: something in difficulties is in disarray, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks a bearded skier who has got into trouble on the slopes how he is getting on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asked' is part of the container signal, not a link: the question word wraps around the scrambled skier.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiskery means having many whiskers, hence somewhat bristly or hairy.

clue.text: Words on holiday? It's on the cards

definitions.text: Words on holiday? It's on the cards

parts.note: surface reading: speech made while away on a break
setter's reading: on the cards is an idiom for likely, but here it means the phrase literally written on postcards

explanation.surface: Something said while away that is quite likely to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the cards' usually means probable; here it means printed on picture postcards sent home from a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the cliché scrawled on holiday postcards to friends and family back home.

clue.text: Practically speaking, fence fit poorly

indicators.note: a thing done poorly is done badly, so these letters are put together wrongly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden fence that has been badly installed, described in a matter-of-fact tone.
explanation.definitionFit: In effect means in practice or virtually, which matches practically speaking as an idiom.

clue.text: A serviceable colour?

parts.note: surface reading: a practical, hard-wearing shade
setter's reading: the colour of the armed services, worn in army uniform

explanation.surface: A question about which shade is practical and hard-wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serviceable' usually means usable, but here it means fit for military service.
explanation.definitionFit: This dull brownish-green is the traditional colour of army uniforms.

clue.text: Cluer's pet bit of fun exceptionally showing deference

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the ordinary, so these letters leave their usual order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here just its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of fun

explanation.surface: The setter's favourite bit of fun is showing respect, a self-referential joke about crossword setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Being respectful means showing regard and deference to someone.

clue.text: Target on ship to shore

parts.note: a butt is a target, as in the butt of a joke
re means on or concerning
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone aims at a ship from the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shore' looks like the coast, but it is the verb meaning to prop up.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttress is to prop up or support, which is the verb sense of shore, as in shoring up a wall.

clue.text: Pass part of the spa (Leamington?) on return

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters run backwards
the answer is just a part of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the last letter of the, all of spa, and the first two letters of Leamington

explanation.surface: A visitor passes through Leamington Spa and comes back again.
explanation.walkthrough: Leamington Spa is a spa town in Warwickshire, England; the parenthesis is decoration to make the surface read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or elapse, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Small-minded person in authority at sea?

definitions.text: Small-minded person in authority at sea

parts.note: petty means narrow and small-minded
an officer holds a post of authority

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded jobsworth who is out of their depth.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces build the rank, and the whole clue then defines it; 'at sea' suggests confusion but places the officer on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty officer is a non-commissioned naval rank, roughly equivalent to an army sergeant.

clue.text: Removed from office because of a fling that went too far?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ousted, as a government or ruler

definitions.text: a fling that went too far
definitions.note: describes the throw itself; the answer is the adjective for a ball so thrown
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ball thrown beyond its target, as in cricket

explanation.surface: A politician ousted after a love affair got out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fling' suggests an affair, but it is a throw; in cricket an overthrow is a throw that misses and runs on past the fielder.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposed ruler has been toppled, and a ball hurled past its target has been thrown too far.

clue.text: Very keen king — not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is left off

parts.note: David was king of Israel

explanation.surface: A monarch who is very enthusiastic, though he is not the first of his name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the first' looks like a regnal number, but it removes the opening letter of DAVID.
explanation.definitionFit: An avid fan is eager and enthusiastic, so the word is a synonym of very keen.

clue.text: A lecture about how to make sore

indicators.note: about suggests being turned around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A talk on how to inflict pain, or a lecture so dull it leaves you aching.
explanation.definitionFit: To ulcerate is to develop or cause open sores, so it means to make sore.

clue.text: Bad guy's row over drink not starting

indicators.note: not starting means the opening letter is missing

parts.note: a racket is a noisy din or row
a common drink

explanation.surface: A villain's argument over drinks that never gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' here is a din, not a line; in a down clue 'over' puts RACKET above the beer, which loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a criminal racket such as extortion, so he is a crook or bad guy.

clue.text: Eccentric split over cup

parts.note: a crack is a split
a pot is a cup, especially a trophy

explanation.surface: An oddball person who has fallen out over a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is a crank or eccentric person with wild ideas.

clue.text: Save jam

definitions.meaning: second meaning: fruit cooked with sugar

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep the jam back for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' reads as an object of save, but it is a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve is to save or protect, and a preserve is a fruit conserve or jam.

clue.text: Fool almost, but a friend

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a chump is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone is nearly an idiot but still a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A chum is an informal word for a close pal or companion.

clue.text: It's limited but fair to take it in

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: fine weather is fair weather
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is restricted, yet it is reasonable to accept that.
explanation.definitionFit: Finite means having bounds or an end, so it is limited.

clue.text: Represent brand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to portray or depict
second meaning: to label or mark out as having a quality

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand' looks like a noun for a product name, but here it is the verb meaning to label someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To characterise is both to portray something and to mark it with a distinctive label, as branding does.

clue.text: Scout around about — about — about — Spain

parts.note: re means about or concerning
c is short for circa, Latin for about
circa again, abbreviated to c
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A stuttering description of someone scouting around Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The three abouts give three short pieces in turn: one from the word re and two from circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce, short for reconnaissance, is a scouting expedition, so to recce is to scout around.

clue.text: Extent of audible moans

indicators.note: audible means able to be heard, so the answer is what the word sounds like

parts.note: sighs are weary moans

explanation.surface: A question of how loud the groaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: Size and extent both mean the dimensions or magnitude of something.

clue.text: Remove left lace top somehow (a footwear tip)

indicators.note: somehow says the order is to be worked out in some way, so the letters are rearranged
remove tells us to take out the letter for left

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Instructions for undoing a shoelace, with a bracketed hint about shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the L out of LACE TOP and rearrange the six letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A toecap is the reinforced covering at the front end of a shoe or boot.

clue.text: One sea ebbing in very large outbreak

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for very large

parts.note: epic means huge in scale
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a tide that is ebbing flows back out, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A single sea retreating during a huge outbreak of disease.
explanation.walkthrough: The Med is the usual crossword shorthand for the Mediterranean; the reversed sea follows the one, and both go inside the very large word.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread outbreak of disease in a community.

clue.text: Upset a French seat

parts.note: un is French for a
a settle is a wooden bench with a high back

explanation.surface: A French chair is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: A settle is an old-fashioned high-backed wooden bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle is to disturb or upset someone's composure.

clue.text: Pupil doesn't start as one who brings home the bacon

definitions.text: one who brings home the bacon

indicators.note: doesn't start means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a learner is a pupil

explanation.surface: A student who fails to begin a job yet ends up supporting the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' could be part of the eye, but here it is a student. To bring home the bacon is to earn the family's living.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing home the bacon is an idiom for making money, so the person doing it is an earner.
